definitions.gloss: Run, Melos! (short story by Dazai Osamu, 1940)
definitions.explanation: A short story by {太宰治|だざいおさむ}, based on a Greek legend retold by Schiller. Melos, sentenced to death by a tyrant king, leaves his best friend as hostage and races back against time to keep his word. A standard text in Japanese middle schools, read as a tale of friendship and trust.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
- The opening line メロス⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{激怒|げきど}→激怒：08681_gekido⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧ (Melos was furious) is famous and often quoted or parodied
- Melos's friend is セリヌンティウス, and the king is ディオニス
- Its upright message contrasts with the dark tone of most of Dazai's work, such as {人間失格|にんげんしっかく}
